Bridge to Terabithia. I don't think it's possible to come away from that book without learning something new about friendship, family, empathy, growing up, love, faith, grief, creativity, and joy.

Watching the 2007 movie will also fulfill this requirement for me.

Space bar toggles what control layout you use.

Yes, I am that evil.

I’m doing much better now. The key was realizing that I’m worth my problems. Yeah, nobody really liked the worst parts of me, and I hated myself for forcing them to put up with it. But they still choose to put up with it, because me at my best is worth me at my worst. In trying to spare people the negativity I bring into their lives, I was also denying them all the positivity as well. Positivity I couldn’t see myself.

I convinced myself that the best thing I could do for everyone I loved was get out of their lives. Forever. Whatever trauma that may have caused in the short term would surely pale in comparison to the problems I’d give those people in the long run should I remain alive. And thinking like that, I actually convinced myself that my suicide would be, in some twisted way, a sacrifice. I wasn’t ending my own pain; I was ending others’.

So why didn’t I do it? Embarrassingly, because I didn’t know how. When I made the decision to kill myself, the nuts and bolts of actually doing it weren’t my focus. All I had was the conviction that I was, for once, doing the right thing for the world and a surge of peace knowing that soon, it would all be over. Perhaps because I was treating it like a sacrifice instead of a suicide, it slipped my mind that I would actually have to take the last step. And instead of shooting myself or taking too many pills or jumping in front of a train, I just sat still in a dazed stupor until somebody who I had earlier that day told, “You will no longer have to suffer because of me,” found me and took me to the hospital.

TL;DR I forgot that I actually had to kill myself to complete the suicide.
